Park & Co Lawyers: 3-Practice Client Self-Help Master Cookbook (FY 2026–27 Verified Edition)

Important Notice: General Legal & Procedural Information Only

This Self-Help Cookbook is published as a complimentary community legal resource by Park & Co Lawyers across Australian Immigration Law, Employment Law, and Family Law to help individuals navigate routine stages on their own first, preventing fee inversion (where early private legal fees exceed or erode your net recovery under Australian Solicitors Conduct Rules r 4.1.1) while clearly highlighting the legal and financial inflection points where specialist representation becomes essential.

  • No Solicitor-Client Relationship: Viewing, downloading, or using this Cookbook does not create a solicitor-client retainer between you and Park & Co Lawyers.
  • Limitation Dates Are Your Responsibility: Park & Co Lawyers does not diarise or monitor statutory limitation periods, visa expiry dates, or Court/Tribunal deadlines prior to formal engagement.
  • Why Self-Calculating Shifts First Protects Your Payout: Fair Work Small Claims up to $100,000 (Fair Work Act s 548) is a strict no-costs jurisdiction (s 570) where the Court generally cannot order the employer to pay your lawyer's fees. Paying hourly legal rates just to add up rosters can consume thousands of dollars of your own back-pay; using our mathematical formulas and companion 208-formula spreadsheet (Park_Co_Underpayment_Self_Calculator_2026_EN.xlsx) lets you preserve 100% of modest claims first.
  • Verification Currency & Official Consultation Guidance: All statutory filing fees, minimum wage figures, and thresholds in this edition are verified against Commonwealth primary .gov.au sources effective 1 July 2026 (FY 2026–27). When an immigration, employment, or family law matter reaches a critical inflection point (Employer Sponsorship, NOICC / PIC 4020 / ART appeals, urgent 21-day visa-linked dismissals, multi-year underpayments above $50,000 or s 550 director liability, or Family Court Consent Orders and formal settlement negotiations), please contact Park & Co Lawyers via https://parklawyers.com.au/links/?lang=en (Chang Min Park, Legal Practitioner Director, Accredited Specialist in Immigration Law, QLS · Email: enquiry@parkcolawyers.com).

1. Why Self-Representation (DIY) Is Often Your Smartest Financial Choice

When a law firm tells you, "Hiring us for this matter would cost you more than it is worth, so you are better off lodging it yourself," that advice reflects strict compliance with Rule 4.1.1 of the Australian Solicitors Conduct Rules (acting in the client's best financial interest).

  1. Preventing Fee Inversion:
  2. Spending $4,500–$8,000 in private legal fees to chase $6,500 in unpaid wages or lodge a routine $195 Visitor Visa leaves you financially worse off even if you succeed.
  3. Australia's Statutory No-Costs Jurisdictions:
  4. Both the Fair Work Commission (FWC) and the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia Small Claims Division (Fair Work Act s 548, claims up to $100,000 · s 570) are statutory no-costs jurisdictions, meaning the losing side generally cannot be ordered to pay your lawyer's fees. Preparing modest claims first with verified calculators and official forms protects 100% of your net recovery.

2. Statutory Limitation Deadlines Across Immigration, Employment & Family Law

Mark these non-negotiable statutory cut-off dates immediately. Missing a jurisdictional deadline by even one day permanently extinguishes your right to apply.

  1. Immigration, ART Merits Review & Judicial Review (Migration Act ss 347, 500, 477):
  2. Standard onshore visa refusal/cancellation: 28 calendar days (weekends and public holidays count).
  3. Applicant in immigration detention: 14 calendar days (the 2025 ART Miscellaneous Measures Act abolished the legacy 2- and 7-working-day detention deadlines).
  4. Onshore s 501 character review (s 500(6B)): 9 calendar days, plus a mandatory 2-business-day pre-hearing evidence bar (s 500(6H)).
  5. Strict Statutory Rule: The ART has zero legal power to extend time. Under s 494C, emailed refusal notices are deemed received at the end of the day transmitted. Federal Court judicial review (s 477) must be filed within 35 days of an ART decision.
  6. Employment Dismissal vs Wage Recovery (Fair Work Act ss 394, 365, 544):
  7. Unfair Dismissal (Form F2) and General Protections Dismissal (Form F8): 21 calendar days after the dismissal takes effect (workplace sexual harassment Form F75 is generally within 24 months; FCFCOA Form 2 after an s 368 certificate is 14 days).
  8. Statutory underpayments of wages, penalty rates, leave, and superannuation (s 548): 6 years from each unpaid payday (s 544). Under Payday Super (effective 1 July 2026), 12% SG contributions must reach the employee's fund within 7 business days of payday.
  9. Family Law Divorce, Property & Maintenance (Family Law Act ss 48, 44):
  10. Online Divorce eligibility: Minimum 12 months + 1 day of continuous separation.
  11. Married couples: 12 months from the date a Divorce Order takes final effect (s 44(3)).
  12. De facto couples: 2 years from the date of separation (s 44(5)).

5. Complex Immigration, Employment & Family Law Matters: When to Consult Park & Co Lawyers

While this Cookbook empowers you to handle routine or small-value matters without fee erosion, self-representation becomes risky once your matter crosses into complex statutory or evidentiary territory:

  • 1. Complex Immigration Matters (QLS Accredited Specialist Representation):
  • Visa cancellation notices (NOICC), PIC 4020 / s 57 natural justice allegations, in-time ART merits reviews (28d / 14d detention / 9d character), s 501 character, PIC 4005/4007 health waivers, unlawful/Bridging Schedule 3 waivers, Employer-Sponsored Visas (SID 482, 186 ENS, 494: CSIT $79,423 · SSIT $146,576 · DAMA $71,481), complex 820/801 Partner Visas, and GSM Case Review ($495) or strategy consultations ($330): https://form.jotform.com/220391121528851
  • 2. Complex Employment & Corporate Matters:
  • Employer / Sponsor Defence & HR Retainers, senior executive or 482/186 visa-linked dismissals (Form F2 / F8 within 21 days), self-calculated major multi-year FCFCOA underpayment & s 550 director liability litigation (> $50,000–$200,000+), and fixed-scope Deed of Release or employment contract reviews: https://form.jotform.com/221642058161853 (For modest wage claims, completing the companion Excel calculator first protects your net recovery.)
  • 3. Complex Family Law Matters:

1. Protecting Your Net Payout: Why Self-Calculating Shifts First Saves You Thousands

Callers inquiring about unpaid wages, cash-in-hand underpayments, unpaid weekend/public holiday penalty rates, or missing superannuation frequently ask: "Can I email you my payslips and rosters so your lawyers can calculate how much my boss owes me?"

At the initial shift-counting stage, engaging a private law firm to manually tally rosters and payslips rarely makes financial sense for a worker. Here is the practical legal economics behind why self-calculating first protects your payout:

  1. Protecting Your Net Recovery (Fair Work Act ss 548, 570):

3. Step 2: Exact Mathematical Self-Calculation Formulas

Perform wage reconciliations in Gross (before-tax) dollars. If you were paid undeclared cash-in-hand with zero PAYG tax remitted to the ATO on your MyGov Income Statement, credit the cash received against your Gross statutory entitlement and note that no PAYG tax was withheld.

Formula 1. Weekly / Fortnightly Shift & Penalty Rate Shortfall

Break every pay period into shift buckets (Ordinary Weekday, Saturday, Sunday, Public Holiday, Overtime First 2h, Overtime >2h, Late-Night/Split-Shift Allowances):

  • Statutory Gross Entitlement: SUM(Actual Hours Worked in Bucket × Applicable FY Award Rate for Bucket) + Applicable Award Allowances
  • Pay-Period Gross Wage Shortfall: MAX(0, Statutory Gross Entitlement − Actual Gross Wages Paid)
Critical Calculation Rule: Never Compound Casual Weekend Penalty RatesDo not multiply the Casual Ordinary Rate ($33.85) by 1.25 for Saturday ($33.85 × 1.25 = $42.31, which is incorrect).Under standard Modern Awards, the 25% casual loading and weekend penalty add together against the Permanent Base Rate (B = $27.08):- Correct Casual Saturday: $27.08 × 150% = $40.62/hr- Correct Casual Sunday: $27.08 × 150% = $40.62/hr ([MA000119] Intro–L2) or $27.08 × 175% = $47.39/hr ([MA000009] Hotel/Pub L2 & [MA000119] L3–L6)

Formula 2. Flat-Rate or Annualised Salary Reconciliation

Even if your contract specifies a flat hourly rate (e.g. "$32/hr all-in") or fixed annual salary (e.g. "$65,000/yr"), an employer cannot legally pay less than the total Modern Award safety net across actual hours, weekends, public holidays, and overtime worked:

  • Salary / Flat-Rate Underpayment: Total Statutory Award Entitlement Across All Actual Shifts − Total Gross Salary Actually Paid
  • (Note: Without an express contractual set-off clause, above-Award weekday payments cannot automatically offset unpaid weekend penalty obligations.)

Formula 3. Accrued Untaken Annual Leave + 17.5% Leave Loading on Termination (NES ss 87, 90(2))

Permanent full-time and part-time employees accrue 4 weeks of paid annual leave per year (4 ÷ 52 = 0.076923 hours per ordinary hour worked, or 152 hours/year on a 38-hour week). Under Fair Work Act s 90(2), untaken annual leave on termination must be paid at the rate payable had the employee taken the leave, including 17.5% Annual Leave Loading where prescribed by the Award:

  • Net Untaken Annual Leave Hours: (Total Ordinary Hours Worked × 4 ÷ 52) − Paid Annual Leave Hours Taken
  • Unpaid Annual Leave Payout: Net Untaken Leave Hours × Final Permanent Base Rate (B) × 1.175

(Note: Untaken Personal/Carer's (sick) leave does not pay out on termination unless an Enterprise Agreement expressly provides for it.)

Formula 4. Payment in Lieu of Notice (NES s 117)

If dismissed without receiving full working notice (excluding casuals and genuine serious misconduct):

  • Minimum Notice Scale: Service ≤ 1 yr: 1 week · > 1–3 yrs: 2 weeks · > 3–5 yrs: 3 weeks · > 5 yrs: 4 weeks
  • Age 45+ Bonus: Add 1 extra week if aged 45 or older with at least 2 years continuous service (maximum 5 weeks).
  • Notice Shortfall: (Statutory Notice Weeks − Working Notice Weeks Given) × Full Weekly Rate of Pay.

Formula 5. NES Redundancy Pay (NES s 119, Employers with 15+ Employees Only)

Applies to permanent employees (≥12 months service) whose job is abolished by a non-small-business employer (15 or more employees across associated entities):

  • 1–<2 yrs: 4 wks · 2–<3 yrs: 6 wks · 3–<4 yrs: 7 wks · 4–<5 yrs: 8 wks · 5–<6 yrs: 10 wks · 6–<7 yrs: 11 wks · 7–<8 yrs: 13 wks · 8–<9 yrs: 14 wks · 9–<10 yrs: 16 wks · 10+ yrs: 12 wks.

Formula 6. Unpaid Superannuation Guarantee (12.0% & 1 July 2026 Payday Super, NES s 116B)

  • Historical & Current SG Rates: FY22–23 = 10.5% · FY23–24 = 11.0% · FY24–25 = 11.5% · From 1 July 2025 (FY25–26 & FY26–27): 12.0%.
  • Ordinary Time Earnings (OTE, ATO SGR 2009/2): Includes ordinary hours, casual loading, weekend/shift penalties, and paid leave taken; excludes true overtime hours and termination lump-sum annual leave payouts.
  • 1 July 2026 Payday Super Reform & NES s 116B Court Recovery:
  • From 1 July 2026, employers must pay 12.0% superannuation with every pay cycle so funds arrive in your super fund within 7 business days of payday.
  • Under NES s 116B, workers can recover unpaid superannuation directly inside an FCFCOA s 548 Small Claim (within the $100,000 cap) in addition to reporting to the ATO (ato.gov.au).
  • Unpaid Super Shortfall: (Statutory OTE × Applicable SG% (12.0%)) − Super Contributions Actually Received by Your Fund.

5. Missing Payslips? Use s 557C Reverse Onus of Proof & The 4-Tier Evidence Checklist

5.1 Payslip & Record-Keeping Breaches (Fair Work Act ss 535–536, reg 3.46) + s 557C Reverse Onus

Employers must keep accurate time and wages records for 7 years (s 535), issue compliant written or electronic payslips within 1 working day of payday (s 536(1)), and never issue knowingly false or misleading payslips (s 536(3)). Under Fair Work Regulations reg 3.46, every payslip must state the employer's legal name and ABN, pay period, payment date, gross and net pay, hourly rate and hours worked, loadings/penalties, deductions, and 12% superannuation amount plus fund name.

  • 3-Step DIY Action Protocol for Payslip Breaches:
  • Send a short written request (citing ss 535–536) asking for all missing payslips and time/wages records within 7 days.
  • Invoke s 557C Reverse Onus of Proof: If the employer failed to keep records or issue payslips without reasonable excuse, the legal burden of proof shifts onto the employer in Court to disprove your reasonable shift reconstruction.
  • Lodge a parallel regulatory breach report at fairwork.gov.au.

5.2 Mandatory 4-Tier Evidence Checklist

  1. Tier 1 (Exact Corporate Entity & s 550 Accessorial Proof): Employment contract, job ad, and abr.business.gov.au ABN/ACN search confirming the exact Pty Ltd legal name (do not sue a shopfront trading name alone), plus texts/emails showing which individual director controlled payroll (s 550).
  2. Tier 2 (Payment & Tax/Super Trail): Highlighted bank statements, any payslips received, MyGov → ATO STP Income Statements, and Super Fund transaction statements.
  3. Tier 3 (Contemporaneous Hours Reconstruction for s 557C): Roster photos, Deputy / Tanda / Square app screenshots (export before losing login access), SMS/WhatsApp shift messages, Google Maps Timeline location exports, public transport card logs, and timestamped opening/closing photos.
  4. Tier 4 (Self-Calculated Schedule): Completed print-out of Park_Co_Underpayment_Self_Calculator_2026_EN.xlsx.

Step 1. Serve a Formal 7-Day Written Letter of Demand

Email your Schedule of Underpayment to the employer (Pty Ltd + Director), citing the exact Modern Award classification, s 536 / s 557C (if payslips were missing), and requesting payment of Gross wages and Super within 7 days, failing which you will file in the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (s 548).

  • Key Box-by-Box Tips: Name the exact Pty Ltd + ACN as Respondent; attach your completed Excel Schedule; claim s 547 pre-judgment interest plus filing-fee reimbursement; serve stamped copies on the ASIC registered office and file an Affidavit of Service.

sections.heading: 3. Step 2: Exact Mathematical Self-Calculation Formulas
sections.text: 3. Step 2: Exact Mathematical Self Calculation Formulas Perform wage reconciliations in Gross (before tax) dollars. If you were paid undeclared cash in hand with zero PAYG tax remitted to the ATO on your MyGov Income Statement, credit the cash received against your Gross statutory entitlement and note that no PAYG tax was withheld.

sections.heading: Formula 1. Weekly / Fortnightly Shift & Penalty Rate Shortfall
sections.text: Formula 1. Weekly / Fortnightly Shift & Penalty Rate Shortfall Break every pay period into shift buckets (Ordinary Weekday, Saturday, Sunday, Public Holiday, Overtime First 2h, Overtime 2h, Late Night/Split Shift Allowances): Statutory Gross Entitlement : SUM(Actual Hours Worked in Bucket × Applicable FY Award Rate for Bucket) + Applicable Award Allowances Pay Period Gross Wage Shortfall : MAX(0, Statutory Gross Entitlement − Actual Gross Wages Paid) Critical Calculation Rule: Never Compound Casual Weekend Penalty Rates Do not multiply the Casual Ordinary Rate ($33.85) by 1.25 for Saturday ($33.85 × 1.25 = $42.31, which is incorrect). Under standard Modern Awards, the 25% casual loading and weekend penalty add together against the Permanent Base Rate (B = $27.08): Correct Casual Saturday : $27.08 × 150% = $40.62/hr Correct Casual Sunday : $27.08 × 150% = $40.62/hr ([MA000119] Intro–L2) or $27.08 × 175% = $47.39/hr ([MA000009] Hotel/Pub L2 & [MA000119] L3–L6)

sections.heading: Formula 2. Flat-Rate or Annualised Salary Reconciliation
sections.text: Formula 2. Flat Rate or Annualised Salary Reconciliation Even if your contract specifies a flat hourly rate (e.g. "$32/hr all in") or fixed annual salary (e.g. "$65,000/yr"), an employer cannot legally pay less than the total Modern Award safety net across actual hours, weekends, public holidays, and overtime worked: Salary / Flat Rate Underpayment : Total Statutory Award Entitlement Across All Actual Shifts − Total Gross Salary Actually Paid (Note: Without an express contractual set off clause, above Award weekday payments cannot automatically offset unpaid weekend penalty obligations.)

sections.heading: Formula 3. Accrued Untaken Annual Leave + 17.5% Leave Loading on Termination (NES ss 87, 90(2))
sections.text: Formula 3. Accrued Untaken Annual Leave + 17.5% Leave Loading on Termination (NES ss 87, 90(2)) Permanent full time and part time employees accrue 4 weeks of paid annual leave per year (4 ÷ 52 = 0.076923 hours per ordinary hour worked, or 152 hours/year on a 38 hour week). Under Fair Work Act s 90(2), untaken annual leave on termination must be paid at the rate payable had the employee taken the leave, including 17.5% Annual Leave Loading where prescribed by the Award: Net Untaken Annual Leave Hours : (Total Ordinary Hours Worked × 4 ÷ 52) − Paid Annual Leave Hours Taken Unpaid Annual Leave Payout : Net Untaken Leave Hours × Final Permanent Base Rate (B) × 1.175 (Note: Untaken Personal/Carer's (sick) leave does not pay out on termination unless an Enterprise Agreement expressly provides for it.)

sections.heading: Formula 4. Payment in Lieu of Notice (NES s 117)
sections.text: Formula 4. Payment in Lieu of Notice (NES s 117) If dismissed without receiving full working notice (excluding casuals and genuine serious misconduct): Minimum Notice Scale : Service ≤ 1 yr: 1 week · 1–3 yrs: 2 weeks · 3–5 yrs: 3 weeks · 5 yrs: 4 weeks Age 45+ Bonus : Add 1 extra week if aged 45 or older with at least 2 years continuous service (maximum 5 weeks). Notice Shortfall : (Statutory Notice Weeks − Working Notice Weeks Given) × Full Weekly Rate of Pay.

sections.heading: 5.1 Payslip & Record-Keeping Breaches (Fair Work Act ss 535–536, reg 3.46) + s 557C Reverse Onus
sections.text: 5.1 Payslip & Record Keeping Breaches (Fair Work Act ss 535–536, reg 3.46) + s 557C Reverse Onus Employers must keep accurate time and wages records for 7 years (s 535), issue compliant written or electronic payslips within 1 working day of payday (s 536(1)), and never issue knowingly false or misleading payslips (s 536(3)). Under Fair Work Regulations reg 3.46, every payslip must state the employer's legal name and ABN, pay period, payment date, gross and net pay, hourly rate and hours worked, loadings/penalties, deductions, and 12% superannuation amount plus fund name. 3 Step DIY Action Protocol for Payslip Breaches : Send a short written request (citing ss 535–536) asking for all missing payslips and time/wages records within 7 days. Invoke s 557C Reverse Onus of Proof: If the employer failed to keep records or issue payslips without reasonable excuse, the legal burden of proof shifts onto the employer in Court to disprove your reasonable shift reconstruction. Lodge a parallel regulatory breach report at [fairwork.gov.au](https://www.fairwork.gov.au).

sections.heading: 5.2 Mandatory 4-Tier Evidence Checklist
sections.text: 5.2 Mandatory 4 Tier Evidence Checklist Tier 1 (Exact Corporate Entity & s 550 Accessorial Proof) : Employment contract, job ad, and [abr.business.gov.au](https://abr.business.gov.au) ABN/ACN search confirming the exact Pty Ltd legal name (do not sue a shopfront trading name alone), plus texts/emails showing which individual director controlled payroll (s 550). Tier 2 (Payment & Tax/Super Trail) : Highlighted bank statements, any payslips received, MyGov → ATO STP Income Statements, and Super Fund transaction statements. Tier 3 (Contemporaneous Hours Reconstruction for s 557C) : Roster photos, Deputy / Tanda / Square app screenshots (export before losing login access), SMS/WhatsApp shift messages, Google Maps Timeline location exports, public transport card logs, and timestamped opening/closing photos. Tier 4 (Self Calculated Schedule) : Completed print out of Park_Co_Underpayment_Self_Calculator_2026_EN.xlsx.

Family Law Self-Help Cookbook: 2025–2026 Reforms Guide to DIY Divorce, Consent Orders & Priority Property Pools (PPP <= $550,000) (FY 2026–27 Verified Edition)

Important Notice: General Legal & Procedural Information Only

This Self-Help Cookbook is published as a complimentary community legal resource by Park & Co Lawyers to help individuals navigate routine family law stages on their own first, preventing fee inversion (where early private legal fees erode the family asset pool under Australian Solicitors Conduct Rules r 4.1.1) while clearly highlighting the legal and financial inflection points where specialist representation becomes essential.

  • No Solicitor-Client Relationship: Viewing, downloading, or using this Cookbook does not create a solicitor-client retainer between you and Park & Co Lawyers.
  • Limitation Dates Are Your Responsibility: Park & Co Lawyers does not diarise or monitor statutory limitation periods, post-divorce property deadlines, or Court deadlines prior to formal engagement.
  • Why Self-Calculating Shifts First Protects Your Payout: Fair Work Small Claims up to $100,000 (Fair Work Act s 548) is a strict no-costs jurisdiction (s 570), so using our companion 208-formula spreadsheet (Park_Co_Underpayment_Self_Calculator_2026_EN.xlsx) lets you preserve 100% of modest wage claims first.
  • Verification Currency & When to Consult Park & Co: All statutory filing fees and thresholds in this edition are verified against Commonwealth primary .gov.au sources effective 1 July 2026 (FY 2026–27). When an immigration, employment, or family law matter reaches a critical inflection point (Employer Sponsorship, NOICC / PIC 4020 / ART appeals, urgent 21-day visa-linked dismissals, multi-year underpayments above $50,000 or s 550 director liability, or Family Court Consent Orders and formal settlement negotiations), please contact us via https://parklawyers.com.au/links/?lang=en (Chang Min Park, Legal Practitioner Director, Accredited Specialist in Immigration Law, QLS · Email: enquiry@parkcolawyers.com).

1. Why Fault-Based Breakup Battles Waste Money: Australia's 3 Family Law Pillars & When to Instruct Park & Co

Callers going through a painful separation sometimes ask lawyers to "prove my ex-partner's infidelity or bad behaviour in court." Under the Family Law Act 1975 (Cth), fault-finding achieves nothing legally and rapidly burns the family asset pool in legal fees. Understanding Australia's three core statutory pillars saves you thousands of dollars:

  1. Pillar 1: Strict No-Fault Divorce (Family Law Act s 48):
  2. Australia has zero fault-based divorce or moral damages. The Court asks only one question: has the marriage broken down irretrievably, proved by 12 months + 1 clear day of separation?
  3. Divorce Does Not Divide Property or Parenting: Once a Divorce Order takes final effect (1 month + 1 day after grant), a strict 12-month clock (s 44(3)) starts ticking to file property/maintenance orders in the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (FCFCOA), or 2 years from separation for de facto couples under s 44(5).
  4. Pillar 2: The 4-Step Property Settlement Framework (ss 79 / 90SM + 10 June 2025 Reforms):
  5. Courts divide assets strictly across four objective steps: (1) identify and value the net global asset, liability, and superannuation pool (both Australian and overseas assets under mandatory Full & Frank Financial Disclosure); (2) assess financial, non-financial, and homemaker/parenting contributions (from 10 June 2025, economic or financial abuse is expressly codified as a statutory factor, alongside specific rules for companion animals / family pets); (3) adjust for future needs (age, health, income disparity, care of children); and (4) ensure the final split is Just and Equitable.
  6. Pillar 3: Parenting (s 60CC Best Interests & Mandatory s 60I Mediation):
  7. Following the 2024–2025 reforms, there is no presumption of equal shared parental responsibility; the Court focuses strictly on six core Best Interests & Safety of the Child factors. Unless urgent family violence or child abuse applies, parents must attempt Family Dispute Resolution (Family Relationship Centre 1800 050 321) and obtain a s 60I Certificate before filing in Court.

1.1 DIY Boundary vs Two High-Value Scenarios Where Park & Co Acts

  • Best Handled via DIY & Public FDR: Emotionally charged fault disputes (use subsidised FDR on 1800 050 321), straightforward Sole or Joint online Divorce applications (comcourts.gov.au), and micro-asset separations.
  • Two Core Scenarios Where You Should Instruct Park & Co via Our Family Law Questionnaire:
  • Track A (Agreement Mostly Reached): You and your former partner have broadly agreed on how to divide property/superannuation or parenting, and need binding Court-sealed Consent Orders ($4,950 fixed-fee package), a Binding Financial Agreement (BFA), or a Binding Child Support Agreement (BCSA) to lock in finality and stamp-duty exemptions.
  • Track B (Bringing a Non-Responsive Ex-Spouse to the Negotiation Table): Your ex-partner is ignoring messages, refusing financial disclosure, or stalling settlement. Park & Co issues a formal Solicitor's Negotiation & Mandatory Full & Frank Financial Disclosure Demand Letter (putting them on notice of adverse costs consequences if they force Court proceedings) to bring them to the settlement table and resolve substantial AU/international pools ($300k–$2M+) or Partner Visa family-violence (Div 1.5) intersections: https://form.jotform.com/262472844554060 (see also https://parklawyers.com.au/blog/2023/07/29857/).

2. DIY Online Divorce (comcourts.gov.au): Incorporating the 10 June 2025 Reforms & 1 July 2026 Fees

  1. Core Eligibility: At least 12 months + 1 clear day of permanent separation (e.g. separated 1 May 2025 → earliest filing date 2 May 2026), plus Australian citizenship, permanent residency, or 12 months ordinary residence.
  2. Major 10 June 2025 Reforms (Family Law Amendment Act 2024):
  3. Short-Marriage Counselling Repealed: Couples married for less than 2 years are no longer required to attend counselling or file a counselling certificate.
  4. Court Attendance Abolished for Most Sole Applicants: Sole applicants with children under 18 no longer need to attend a court hearing unless the respondent files an objection or substituted/dispensed service is sought.
  5. Verified Filing Fees (Effective 1 July 2026):
  6. Full Divorce Filing Fee: $1,170
  7. Reduced Fee (eligible concession card / financial hardship): $390
  8. Joint Application Trap: On a Joint Application, both spouses must hold eligible concession cards to receive the $390 reduced fee; if only one spouse holds a card, the full $1,170 fee applies.
  9. Separation Under One Roof & Sole Service Rules:
  10. Separation Under One Roof: Requires an Affidavit explaining separate sleeping, finances, domestic duties, and public notification (Sole = Applicant Affidavit + 1 independent adult witness Affidavit; Joint = separate Affidavits from both spouses).
  11. Sole Service (Divorce Service Kit): Never hand divorce papers to your spouse yourself. An adult third party (18+) or process server must serve the respondent at least 28 days before hearing (within Australia) or 42 days (overseas), completing Acknowledgment of Service, Affidavit of Service, and Affidavit Proving Signature.

3. Consent Orders ($215) & Priority Property Pools (PPP <= $550,000)

  1. Application for Consent Orders ($215 filing fee):
  2. Informal written agreements have zero binding finality under the Family Law Act and risk later challenges (or setting aside under s 79A if assets are concealed).
  3. Mandatory Superannuation Split Rule: You must serve the proposed Minute on the Superannuation Fund Trustee at least 28 days before filing to obtain written procedural fairness confirmation.
  4. Identical .docx Rule: Upload both the signed PDF Minute and a word-for-word identical editable .docx Minute, plus a Notice of Child Abuse, Family Violence or Risk if parenting orders are sought.
  5. Contested Small Pools: Priority Property Pools (PPP <= $550,000):
  6. Where net property excluding superannuation is $550,000 or less, use the streamlined PPP Financial Summary alongside an Initiating Application (1 July 2026 fees: Financial or Parenting Final = $455 / $610 with Interim; Both = $740 / $895 with Interim).
  7. Parenting Pre-Action (s 60I Certificate) & Page Limits: Unless urgent family violence or child abuse applies, obtain an FDR s 60I Certificate first (e.g. via Family Relationship Centre 1800 050 321). Interim affidavits are capped at 10 pages.

4. Complex Family Law Matters: Securing Binding Finality With Park & Co Lawyers

While online Divorce applications are straightforward to self-file, drafting errors in property or parenting settlements trigger Court requisitions, forfeit stamp-duty exemptions, or leave your future income exposed:

  • Fixed-Fee Property & Parenting Consent Orders ($4,950 Package) & BCSA: We convert your amicable agreement into Court-sealed Consent Orders, including mandatory 28-day Superannuation Trustee procedural fairness clearance.

sections.heading: 1. Why Fault-Based Breakup Battles Waste Money: Australia's 3 Family Law Pillars & When to Instruct Park & Co
sections.text: 1. Why Fault Based Breakup Battles Waste Money: Australia's 3 Family Law Pillars & When to Instruct Park & Co Callers going through a painful separation sometimes ask lawyers to "prove my ex partner's infidelity or bad behaviour in court." Under the Family Law Act 1975 (Cth), fault finding achieves nothing legally and rapidly burns the family asset pool in legal fees. Understanding Australia's three core statutory pillars saves you thousands of dollars: Pillar 1: Strict No Fault Divorce (Family Law Act s 48) : Australia has zero fault based divorce or moral damages. The Court asks only one question: has the marriage broken down irretrievably, proved by 12 months + 1 clear day of separation? Divorce Does Not Divide Property or Parenting: Once a Divorce Order takes final effect (1 month + 1 day after grant), a strict 12 month clock (s 44(3)) starts ticking to file property/maintenance orders in the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (FCFCOA), or 2 years from separation for de facto couples under s 44(5). Pillar 2: The 4 Step Property Settlement Framework (ss 79 / 90SM + 10 June 2025 Reforms) : Courts divide assets strictly across four objective steps: (1) identify and value the net global asset, liability, and superannuation pool (both Australian and overseas assets under mandatory Full & Frank Financial Disclosure); (2) assess financial, non financial, and homemaker/parenting contributions (from 10 June 2025, economic or financial abuse is expressly codified as a statutory factor, alongside specific rules for companion animals / family pets); (3) adjust for future needs (age, health, income disparity, care of children); and (4) ensure the final split is Just and Equitable. Pillar 3: Parenting (s 60CC Best Interests & Mandatory s 60I Mediation) : Following the 2024–2025 reforms, there is no presumption of equal shared parental responsibility; the Court focuses strictly on six core Best Interests & Safety of the Child factors. Unless urgent family violence or child abuse applies, parents must attempt Family Dispute Resolution (Family Relationship Centre 1800 050 321) and obtain a s 60I Certificate before filing in Court.

Major 10 June 2025 Reforms ( Family Law Amendment Act 2024 ): Short Marriage Counselling Repealed: Couples married for less than 2 years are no longer required to attend counselling or file a counselling certificate. Court Attendance Abolished for Most Sole Applicants: Sole applicants with children under 18 no longer need to attend a court hearing unless the respondent files an objection or substituted/dispensed service is sought. Verified Filing Fees (Effective 1 July 2026) : Full Divorce Filing Fee: $1,170 Reduced Fee (eligible concession card / financial hardship): $390 Joint Application Trap: On a Joint Application, both spouses must hold eligible concession cards to receive the $390 reduced fee; if only one spouse holds a card, the full $1,170 fee applies. Separation Under One Roof & Sole Service Rules : Separation Under One Roof: Requires an Affidavit explaining separate sleeping, finances, domestic duties, and public notification (Sole = Applicant Affidavit + 1 independent adult witness Affidavit; Joint = separate Affidavits from both spouses). Sole Service (Divorce Service Kit): Never hand divorce papers to your spouse yourself. An adult third party (18+) or process server must serve the respondent at least 28 days before hearing (within Australia) or 42 days (overseas), completing Acknowledgment of Service, Affidavit of Service, and Affidavit Proving Signature.

disambiguators.title: Which Food / Hospitality Award Covers My Workplace? (4-Way Split)
items: Standalone table-service restaurants, Korean BBQ, dine-in cafes → Restaurant Award [MA000119] (Casual Sunday is 150% [$40.62] for Intro-L2, jumping to 175% at L3-L6.)
Counter-order / takeaway-predominant fried chicken, bubble tea, sushi kiosks, burger/pizza outlets → Fast Food Award [MA000003] (Higher L1 base: $27.81 FT / $34.76 Cas.)
Hotels, pubs, resorts, casinos & hotel housekeeping → Hospitality (General) Award [MA000009] (Casual Sunday is 175% [$47.39 at L2] across all grades.)
In-store retail bakeries → General Retail [MA000004]; wholesale non-retail bakeries, central kitchens & kimchi/dumpling plants → Food Mfg [MA000073] (Compounded 187.5%/250% casual weekend).

disambiguators.title: Paid on an ABN (Day Rate, Per-Car, Per-Class or Commission): Am I Really an Employee?
items: Fair Work Act s 15AA ('Real Substance, Practical Reality & True Nature'): Even if you signed an ABN contractor agreement, courts assess practical control over rosters/hours, inability to delegate, use of the business's branding/equipment, and lack of independent goodwill.

7 High-Risk Sham-ABN Sectors: (1) Tiling, gyprock, painting & site labour (MA000020), (2) Contract office/mall cleaning (MA000022), (3) Car wash/detailing (MA000089), (4) Hair/nail/lash commission (MA000005), (5) Per-class Pilates/PT studios (MA000094), (6) Rostered NDIS support (MA000100), (7) Fixed-run delivery vans (MA000038).

Recoverable Back-Pay (Up to 6 Years): Award base, weekend/night/overtime shortfalls, accrued annual leave (if non-casual), 12% Superannuation (SGAA s 12(3)), plus s 357 sham-contracting civil penalties.

disambiguators.title: All-In Salaries, Cert III Cook Under-Classification & 482 Cashback Traps
items: No Cross-Period Salary Pooling (FWO v Woolworths / Coles [2025] FCA 1092): All-in salaries cannot offset underpayments in busy pay periods using 'surplus' pay from quieter periods: every single pay cycle must satisfy the Award, and employers must keep s 535 overtime records.

Mandatory Cert III Cook Floor (FWO v Sushi Bay (No 2) [2024] FCA 76; $15.3M penalties in [2024] FCA 869): Any cook holding AQF Certificate III in Commercial Cookery performing cooking duties must be paid at least Level 4 (Cook Grade 3: $29.45 FT / $36.81 Cas).
Unlawful Visa Cashbacks (s 325) & Dual Rates: Demanding cash kickbacks for 482/186 sponsorship or falsifying payslips triggers s 557A serious-contravention liability.

disambiguators.title: Roster Cut to Zero After Raising Pay Concerns? (21-Day Dismissal Clock)
items: Full Bench Authority (Dea Chang Kim v The Marlow Family Trust No 3 [2026] FWCFB 227): Abruptly cutting a regular casual's shifts to zero or removing them from roster chats can constitute an employer-initiated dismissal (s 386(1)(a)).

Strict 21-Calendar-Day Deadline: Both Unfair Dismissal (Form F2) and General Protections Dismissal (Form F8: zero minimum service required if dismissed for inquiring about pay/payslips) MUST be lodged within 21 calendar days of dismissal taking effect.

FORMULAS 1 & 2 · WAGES & SALARY
Shift Penalty & Flat-Rate Reconciliation
• Statutory Gross = SUM(Actual Hours in Bucket x Applicable FY Rate) + Allowances
• Pay-Period Shortfall = MAX(0, Statutory Gross - Actual Gross Paid)
• Flat rates (e.g. '$30/hr all-in') or fixed salaries cannot pay below total Modern Award entitlements in any single pay period.
FORMULAS 3, 4 & 5 · LEAVE & NOTICE
Annual Leave (+17.5%) · Notice · Redundancy
• Annual Leave Payout (s 90(2)) = ((Ordinary Hours x 4 / 52) - Leave Taken) x Base (B) x 1.175
• Notice in Lieu (s 117): 1–4 wks by service (+1 extra wk if age >=45 & >=2 yrs, max 5 wks)
• Redundancy (s 119): 4–16 wks for permanent staff at employers with >=15 staff
FORMULA 6 · 12% PAYDAY SUPER
12.0% SG & 1 July 2026 Payday Super
• Unpaid Super = (Statutory OTE (excl. overtime & leave lump sums) x 12.0%) - Super Received in Fund
• Payday Super (from 1 Jul 2026): Due in fund within 7 business days of each payday.
• Directly recoverable in Court Small Claims under NES s 116B.
